title: Livepatch: conservative preemptive eviction + tracing rollout to mitigate Hosted/Dedicated/Private GPU OOM spikes
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Multiple P0 customer escalations across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments showing GPU OOM cascades tied to KV cache state corruption and memory fragmentation. This ticket tracks a conservative livepatch that introduces an earlier preemptive eviction pass plus a short-lived diagnostic tracing mode to capture per-session KV liveness for postmortem. Goals: stop immediate OOM cascades, gather deterministic traces for root-cause, and stage a follow-up compaction/checksum resync. Scope: hosted API pools (primary), Dedicated reserved pools (staged), Private on-prem lab (validation before customer patch). Approach: (1) implement eviction-only livepatch that lowers eviction thresholds and enforces synchronous tombstone reclamation in the hot path; (2) enable diagnostic trace sampling (0.5% by default) that writes compact KV liveness blobs to encrypted storage; (3) ship feature flags and per-tenant knobs; (4) canary rollout with automated SLO checks and rollback. Trade-offs: earlier eviction can increase p95 generation latency for very long sequences and may cause cache miss amplification; we accept this temporarily to prevent customer-visible OOMs. Follow-ups: compaction + checksum-resync patch (requires more invasive index surgery and a security review), long-term telemetry dashboards, and an ops-runbook for future escalations.
comments: 2025-02-18 - 09:14 - Maya Chen: Initial triage: multiple customer escalations (INC-4721, INC-4729) across Hosted and Dedicated pools reporting sudden GPU OOM cascades correlated with KV cache growth on long-tail sessions. Reproduced in perf-lab by driving 600 concurrent long-context sessions. Observed fragmentation + stale KV tombstones delaying reclamation. Hypothesis: concurrent eviction + index update races create phantom allocations that prevent slab reuse.

2025-02-18 - 13:40 - Liam O'Neal: Proposed mitigation: implement a livepatch that introduces a conservative preemptive eviction pass (earlier threshold trigger) and a diagnostic trace mode to capture per-session KV liveness metadata. Patch is feature-flagged per-pool and per-tenant; minimal allocations in hot path. Draft PR planned.

2025-02-19 - 10:05 - Eng lead (R. Patel): Two-phased rollout approved. Phase 1 = eviction-only + telemetry. Phase 2 = compaction + checksum resync if traces point to index desync. Decision rationale: minimize code surface for immediate rollbackability. Note: coordinate with Dedicated upgrade window and Private lab to avoid customer downtime.

2025-02-20 - 16:22 - QA (S. Alvarez): Canary run hosted-canary-3 for 24h with eviction threshold lowered by 15% saw OOM rate drop from 12/hr -> 0.9/hr. Token p95 increased by ~6ms on long sequences. No KV corruption observed in traces; 0.7% of sessions triggered a resync event (expected).

2025-02-22 - 09:11 - Security (L. Wong): Verified diagnostic traces exclude user payloads and secrets. Artifacts encrypted at rest with KMS and TTL=7d. Security sign-off not required for eviction-only path; compaction path will require formal review.

2025-02-23 - 18:02 - Ops (K. Rao): PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1842. Added ops-runbook: playbook/oom_surge_mitigation_v1.md describing detection alerts, manual rollback steps, and emergency tenant-quarantine. Rollout plan: region-by-region with automated rollback if OOM reduction < 80% in 2h window or if p95 token latency increases > 25%.

2025-02-25 - 11:45 - Liam O'Neal: Canary metrics stable on hosted-canary-3 and dedicated-canary-1. Approved wider staged rollout to Private lab nodes for 48h. Next action: schedule customer patch window, prepare non-disruptive compaction follow-up PR after traces analysed.
